title: Project gap persister deletes repo-owned .bbox/gaps files it didn't create
wanted_capability: The project-scope gap persister should merge unknown on-disk .bbox/gaps/*.json files into its store (or at minimum never delete files it didn't write) when persisting. Today it rewrites the directory from its in-memory project store: gap files that exist on disk but not in the store — e.g. records migrated from global scope whose authoritative copy is the committed repo file (gap-79a3edef, gap-98d35225, migrated 2026-06-11 with global twins resolved as "authoritative record is the project-scoped file") — are silently deleted on the next project-scoped bbox_gap call from any session. This clobbers committed repo-owned knowledge and shows up as confusing unstaged deletions in peer worktrees. A migration/import path (scope=global → project) that registers the project record in the daemon store atomically with writing the file would close the desync at the source.
fallback_used: git restore the deleted files from HEAD after each clobber; the records survive only because they were committed
notes: Reproduced live 2026-06-11: this session's project-scoped bbox_gap filings triggered the persist that deleted both files (restored via git restore). Fix deployed to prod daemon same day (a9b00cf, redeployed + verified): repo files now parse (updated_at defaulted) and the purge refuses to delete unknown ids — post-restart, gap-79a3edef/gap-98d35225 load project-scoped and survive project gap writes.
resolution_note: Fixed in a9b00cf: GapNote.updated_at is now serde-defaulted (backfilled from created_at at repo-file load) so peer/hand-authored files parse, and the save-side purge takes the store's full known-id set and refuses to delete any on-disk gap file whose id it does not hold. Regression tests cover the incident repro, unparseable-file protection, and the legitimate reassignment purge. NOTE: the running prod daemon predates the fix — it keeps clobbering gap-79a3edef/gap-98d35225 on every project gap write until rebuilt/restarted (operator-gated; next daily cleaning covers it).
